sentences.sentence: **Headline:** California Prosecutors Allege Police Chief and Five Colleagues Engaged in Vehicle Impound Scandal

**King City, CA** - The prosecutor in a rural California agricultural community says that police officers there preyed upon the poor, impounding their cars then selling the vehicles when the owners couldn't afford the fees.
Six officers, including the former police chief of King City and his interim successor, have been arrested and charged in connection with the alleged scheme.

According to Monterey County District Attorney, Dean Flippo, the officers would impound the cars of individuals who were unable to pay release fees, and then turn the vehicles over to the owner of the local impound lot.
The impound lot owner would then transfer the cars to the police department, which would sell or keep them.
Flippo alleges that the officers' actions were motivated by a desire to pad their own pockets, rather than to uphold the law.
"They were using their power to prey on vulnerable members of our community, people who were struggling to get by," Flippo said in a statement.
The arrested officers include former Police Chief Dennis Swanson, Interim Police Chief Bruce Miller, and four other current and former officers.
Miller, who is now facing charges, has denied any wrongdoing.
"I did nothing wrong," Miller told a CNN affiliate in an interview.
However, the same affiliate reported that the small police department in King City is strained by the number of arrests and is struggling to maintain services.
The alleged scandal has left many in the community reeling, with some calling for the officers' immediate termination.
"This is a betrayal of trust, plain and simple," said one local resident, who wished to remain anonymous.
"We expect our law enforcement officers to uphold the law, not to break it."
The investigation, which was launched in 2013, is ongoing.
Charges have been filed, but the full extent of the alleged scheme remains to be seen.

A Florida teenager attacked and set on fire last month, allegedly by five teenage friends, was undergoing skin graft surgery Friday, the first procedure in his recovery, a hospital spokeswoman said.

Michael Brewer, 15, who was attacked on October 12 at a Townhouses complex in Deerfield Beach, has been in guarded condition and is expected to return to the intensive care unit after the surgery, according to reports.
The teenager suffered severe burns to over 65 percent of his body in the incident, which left him fighting for his life.
The complex attack has sparked widespread concern and outrage among the community, with the accused teenagers facing serious charges.
Three of the five teenagers accused of setting Brewer on fire have pleaded not guilty to the charge of attempted murder.
The remaining two suspects are still expected to enter their pleas in the coming days.
Brewer's long and arduous road to recovery is expected to be marked by multiple surgeries and extensive physical therapy.
The young boy's family is staying hopeful for his recovery despite the severity of the injuries.
The skin graft surgery, which was performed at the Bethesda Memorial Hospital in Boynton Beach, is the first step in a lengthy recovery process for Brewer.
The exact details of the surgery were not disclosed by hospital officials, but it is known that it involved transferring Brewer's own skin to the burned areas to aid in the healing process.
The investigation into the attack is ongoing, and authorities have yet to release any additional details about the events surrounding the incident.
However, officials have confirmed that the incident was a result of a disagreement among Brewer and the five accused teenagers.
As Brewer continues his fight for recovery, his family and the community are rallying around him, offering their support and well-wishes for his speedy recovery.
**Genealogist Tries to Fill Out Details of Doomed Civil War Submarine Crew**
One investigative tip can lead to another -- and another.
Linda Abrams, a genealogy gumshoe, went to Texas to match handwriting samples.
She spent a couple weeks in Kentucky following a tip, only to find it was just hearsay.
Hunley, a Civil War submarine that sank off the coast of South Carolina in 1864 after sinking a Union vessel.
The sub and its eight-man crew were never recovered, leaving behind a legacy of uncertainty and curiosity.
Since the Hunley's discovery in 1995, researchers have been trying to identify the sailors who perished with the sub.
However, DNA matches have been elusive, with only one confirmed match found so far.
The individual's DNA profile was matched to a descendant of a known crew member, but this lone identification leaves a significant gap in understanding the lives and experiences of the crew.
One particular enigma is the captain's possible connection to a romantic interest, who allegedly gave him a gold coin.
Although this rumor has been passed down through generations, no conclusive evidence has been found to prove it.
Undeterred by the lack of concrete evidence, Abrams is driven by her passion for genealogical detective work.
"Each small lead gives me a new path to explore," she says.
"I'm not giving up on finding more DNA matches or verifying the captain's gold coin story."
Her relentless pursuit has taken her from historical archives to living descendants, gathering every shred of information that might reveal the secrets of the Hunley's doomed crew.
The investigation is a testament to the power of dedication and the human desire to learn from history.
With the nation approaching the 160th anniversary of the Hunley's sinking, Abrams' quest serves as a poignant reminder of the sacrifices made by the crew during a pivotal moment in American history.
Defender Per Mertesacker has called on Arsenal to show their Barclays Premier League challenge is very much 'alive' when they head to West Brom for Saturday's lunchtime kick-off.
The Gunners produced a much-improved, composed display in their previous outing, but still find themselves in eighth place, a long way off the league leaders.

Despite a promising campaign last season, Arsenal have been unimpressive so far this term, and Mertesacker acknowledges that things need to pick up quickly if the team is to retain any hope of securing the title.
However, the veteran defender is adamant that his side still have what it takes to mount a serious challenge.
"We know that our Premier League challenge is still alive and we want to show that we can win the league," Mertesacker said in a statement.
"We've been inconsistent so far, but we've shown glimpses of what we're capable of.
Now it's about putting it all together and getting the results that we need."
Arsenal will look to take that next step when they travel to the Hawthorns to face West Brom on Saturday.
The Baggies, currently 12th in the table, have been struggling for form themselves, and Mertesacker sees an opportunity for his team to pick up a much-needed three points.
"We've been in situations like this before, and we know that we have the players and the quality to come out on top," he said.
"We just need to focus on our own game, and try to get the win.
We can't control what the other teams do, but we can control how we perform, and that's what we're going to try to do."
With their Premier League challenge still very much alive, Arsenal will be looking to get back on track and start climbing the table.

On an extra point attempt, kicker Keegen Hemenway was disappointed when the ball sailed through the air, seemingly destined for the ground.

However, in a bizarre and hilarious turn of events, the ball took an unexpected path, bouncing off the helmet of a Milbank High School defender and arcing through the uprights for an apparent two-point conversion.
The astonishing moment took place during a game between Dell Rapids and Milbank High School, which ultimately ended with a resounding 51-0 victory for the Dell Rapids team.
The score that started it all, the freak 'own goal', left the Dell Rapids fans stunned and the Milbank team in awe.
The video, recorded by a spectator, has since been uploaded to YouTube, garnering close to 400,000 views in a matter of days.
The clip has been widely shared on social media, with many using the hashtag #OwnGoal to comment on the absurdity of the situation.
Reactions range from amusement to shock, but one thing is clear: this unusual sequence of events will be etched in the memories of football fans for a long time to come.
As the game progressed, Dell Rapids took advantage of the momentum and went on to secure a commanding 51-0 lead, effectively sealing the win.
**Location-Based Dating Apps See Huge Growth, Reaching 91 Million Users Worldwide**
Location-based dating apps, such as Tinder and the League, have a combined total of 91 million users.
Now a new study has found that nearly two thirds of these app users are men – and one in five will pay for premium services.
The study reveals that a staggering 66% of users of location-based dating apps are men, while 34% are women.
Furthermore, it has been discovered that 21% of users are willing to pay for premium services, a significant figure in an industry where free and paid versions of apps often coexist.
According to the research, mobile dating app users are predominantly young adults, with 16- to 34-year-olds making up the majority.
This demographic accounts for over 70% of all mobile dating app users.
The study also found that six per cent of web users currently use a location-based dating app, indicating that online dating is becoming increasingly mainstream.
Tinder, one of the leading location-based dating apps, has revealed that its users log on to the app on average 11 times a day.
Women use the app for around 8.5 minutes per session, swiping through potential matches, while men spend around 7.2 minutes per session.
The growing popularity of location-based dating apps has led to a rise in usage among various demographics.
However, it remains to be seen whether these figures will translate into successful relationships, or if users are simply using the apps as a way to meet new people and have casual interactions.
As the dating app landscape continues to evolve, it is clear that location-based dating apps are becoming an increasingly important part of modern dating culture.
A plane performing at an air show in Davenport, Iowa, crashed and exploded in front of thousands of spectators.
The pilot of the plane was killed in the accident Saturday afternoon when the plane nosedived into an alfalfa field during the Quad City Air Show.

According to eyewitnesses, the plane, a Pitts Special S-2S, a custom-built aerobatic aircraft, was performing a routine maneuver when it suddenly lost altitude and crashed into the field near the riverfront area of downtown Davenport.
The impact was followed by a massive explosion that sent debris flying across the field.
A home video, shot by a witness who wished to remain anonymous, captured the horrific scene.
The footage shows the plane plummeting towards the ground before it crashes into the field, followed by a large explosion that engulfs the wreckage.
The video has sparked a mix of shock and horror among viewers.
"We were standing right across the field, and it was like a nightmare unfolding before our eyes," said Jane Smith, a witness who was in attendance.
"The plane just dropped out of the sky, and it was like slow motion.
We couldn't believe what we were seeing."
Despite the chaos, witnesses say that emergency responders were on the scene quickly, and nearby buildings were evacuated as a precaution.
The cause of the crash is still unknown, and an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is underway.
The pilot's identity has not been released by authorities, pending notification of next of kin.
The NTSB will work to determine the cause of the crash, as well as the circumstances leading up to it.
The Quad City Air Show, which features a variety of aircraft performing aerobatic stunts, was in its final day of performances when the accident occurred.
Samsung Files Design Patent for Wearable Computer Glasses with a Twist
Samsung has filed a design patent for wearable computer glasses that are tethered to a smartphone.
The Samsung spectacle plugs into a mobile phone and displays information such as text messages and phone calls.
Unlike Google Glass, which is wireless, the new design is expected to have a longer lifespan and be lighter than the popular smart glasses.
According to sources, Samsung calls the new wearable computer glasses a'sports glass', indicating that it is primarily designed for athletes and fitness enthusiasts.

One of the key features of the device is its ability to allow users to 'take phone calls and listen to music during workouts', making it a convenient accessory for those who enjoy staying connected while on the move.
The design patent suggests that Samsung doesn't intend for users to wear the'sports glass' all day, every day.
Instead, it appears to be a device that is meant to be used for specific activities or occasions, such as working out or engaging in sports.
However, one major downside to the device is its reliance on a constant cable connection to a smartphone.
Users will need to keep their phone nearby and be connected to the cable at all times, which could be restrictive for some users.
Despite this limitation, the design patent for Samsung's'sports glass' could have significant implications for the wearable technology industry.

The company's emphasis on durability and lightness is a departure from the more fragile and complex design of Google Glass, and could potentially make the device more appealing to a wider range of consumers.
As the wearable technology market continues to evolve, it will be interesting to see how Samsung's'sports glass' design is received by consumers and competitors alike.

Former US President Barack Obama has made a tongue-in-cheek remark about his public disagreements with Republican politicians, and it appears to be working in his favor.
"It is always good publicity for a Republican if they're in an argument with me," Obama said in a recent interview.
While his statement may have been intended as a lighthearted jab, it seems to have had an unexpected consequence.
One Republican who has clearly benefited from a public disagreement with Obama is Arizona Governor Jan Brewer.
Brewer's memoir, 'Scorpions for Breakfast: My Fight Against Special Interests, Liberal Media, and Cynical Politics,' was released in 2011.
However, since the governor publicly criticized Obama's healthcare reform, sales of her book have seen a significant surge.
Brewer famously clashed with Obama in 2010 when she blocked a group of protesters from interfering with the President's meeting with her at the White House.
The governor's defiant stance against Obama's healthcare reforms was widely reported in the media, and it appears that this controversy has helped boost her book sales.
Although Obama's statement may be intended as a subtle boast about his ability to generate publicity, it also highlights the enduring appeal of politics in American life.
For some politicians, a public spat with a high-profile figure like Obama can be a PR goldmine, even if it's not always intentional.
The sales figures for Brewer's book are a testament to the enduring power of controversy in the world of politics.
Whether Obama's statement was meant as a boast or not, it's clear that his public disagreements continue to captivate the public's attention and drive book sales.
